newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close stronger, aided by golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close stronger, aided by golds.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed stronger in moderate trading on Friday, hiking higher by the extended rally in heavyweight golds.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 21.88 points to 6226.95 on turnover of 136.07 million shares worth C$1.97 billion.
"The interest with the gold sector is still occupying a lot of attention," said ScotiaMcLeod senior vice-president Fred Ketchen.
Bullion prices continued to bounce back from recent lows. April COMEX rose $1.50 an ounce to close at $354.10.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, all climbed except for two -- retail and banks.
Golds led the gainers, followed by conglomerates, transportation and forestry products.
Advancing issues outpaced declines 587 to 434 and another 280 traded flat.
Over the week, Canada's largest equities market only rose 21 points from Monday's open, trading in a relatively narrow range.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd lost 1.50 to reach 21.20 after investors tried to sort through this week's news.

Stakeholders read a report that Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan said Bre-X had to consult its Indonesian partners before selling its stake. However chief executive David Walsh said Bre-X, which holds its stake through a wholly owned unit, could receive a third-party bid without offering its partners including Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc rights of first refusal.
